G: One of the happy guys. G lends a hand, he smiles and he laughs more than most, and all this macho crap too many men seem to put on is basically none of his business. But, he's no sissy.
Gabe: An energetic, kind and busy young man who darts about the world with a strange kind of athletic elegance.
Gabriel: A serious fellow with brooding looks and dark hair.
Gage: City dweller. He knows most of the shortcuts around town, his first reaction is to look serious rather than to smile (which, for some reason unbeknown to us, many girls find quite attractive) and he takes a while to let his guard down. He always gives the impression he’s about to leave.
Gareth: Yes, one r, two r's, it doesn't really matter G. Check out Garreth. You two are cut from the same chunk of whatever it is you're made from. (We're still waiting for the geology reports to come back.)
Garfield: Yes, he exists in the flesh. At work he’s surprisingly attentive and competent, but out here in civilian-land he’s a funny ratbag, as you’d expect. Old ladies just want to cuddle him up and stick him in their handbag.
Garret: Calm. At peace. Garret is the kind of man who, as a lone father, would have no reservations at taking his two young children on a three month tour of India.
Garreth: Garreth is purposeful with a giant intellect. Yes, the undertow of a hidden ego lurks here but make no mistake, Garreth is capable of absolute greatness…not that you’re ever likely to hear about it.
Garrick: A likely lad who believes life is short.
Garrie: It is of some small surprise for those who meet Garrie that he is not as laconic as his close cousins (below) and definitely more educated. Not pigeon-holed into a life of manual labour, Garrie has artistic edges which means anything is possible, although he is reasonably tired of having to correct the spelling of his name.
Garry: (Yeah, I know - there are two R's in your name but suck it up sunshine.) There’s a red wine stain on the lounge room carpet that you/he left one night after he/you turned up drunk and unannounced. Moral to the story: if you've had a few and you get a rush of blood for a visit, do us a favour and just give us a ring beforehand, eh? Thanks. Management.
Garth: As a pick-up line to a girl, he’ll say, “......umm...do you wanna’ go outside....and umm....check out your pool?” By the end of saying it even he is visibly wincing at how pathetic it sounds.
Gary: There’s a red wine stain on the lounge room carpet that he left one night after he turned up drunk and unannounced.
Gator: Gator doesn’t live in Zurich or Chicago or Stockholm because he’s better suited to a much warmer clime. This doesn’t stop him from planning well, however, and he therefore tends to do things properly, wasting no or little energy in the process.
Gav: Whether he’s a large dopey bloke from Miami, who watches a heap of TV and puts away at least half a case of beer each night, an eccentric gay hairdresser from Tasmania, who is as fun and famous as he is dangerous, or a mild-mannered engineer from Helsinki, who somehow ended up running the company, Gav is a cool cat who is loved and appreciated by literally everyone.
Gavin: Elemental. Gavin is genuine and ostensibly tranquil.
Gayne: Gayne isn't the sort of personality to be affected by pressure or stress. Yes he has his moments, but by and large he is able to see his way around tight moments and corners, rarely getting flustered. He is no fun for his kids to argue with because he barely raises his voice, and therefore never shows signs that their actions are bothersome.
Gazza: Another who needs no introduction. Gazza is friendly to strangers and forgetful when it comes to things that aren’t in front of his face. As a physical fellow who prefers to use his hands, Gazza enjoys the satisfaction of physically watching a project have a start, a middle and an end. Facebook is rarely any of his business. Gazza is a champ, make no mistake.
Ged: Ged is indestructible, paradoxical, sarcastic and sufficiently enigmatic.
Geeves: Ever seen the group-orgy scene in the movie, ‘Eyes Wide Shut’? Well, in the real world, Geeves organises these things for a living.
Gene: The captain of the team, the founder of the company and a leader when a vaccum appears. Will he break the rules? If he thinks they are not worthy, sure. Indeed, his arrogance is something to be lauded not feared. Someone has to trailblaze. (Don't forget, however, that Gene can be a big softie as well.)
Geoff: Regardless if he owns a construction company or is involved in the conservation movement, this fellow is basically rock-solid with the odd sprinkle of greatness at the edges. (He is unique in the car world for his renowned reliability.)
Geordie: Georgie is one of those Navy Captains who is liked by his crew. He's good at his job, which is one thing, and he has a rather laid-back demeanour, which they appreciate because it means they can talk to him, but he commands respect because when the shit hits the fan his orders are clear and consice, his course of action is generally correct and, touch wood, they know he'd be the one to go down with the ship if he had to.
George: Plonk goes the dollop of cream on top of the apple pie.
Georgie: Never without a multitude of friends, Georgie is a big kid at heart who, at the tender age of 55, is liable to have a very young wife.
Gerald: A lovely old fellow that lives on his own and plays the piano in the nude.
Gerard: As a young man he was once kicked out of a nightclub for trying to sneak into the girl’s toilet and watch one of them take a pee, but not long after that he discovered God and became determined to cleanse himself of such damnations. Today, as a man of the cloth, he often wears a funny white gown and speaks in dramatic tones with his hands held in the air, in the same way that a doctor walks into an operating theatre having just washed them. Very odd.
Gerhard: Gerhard rarely attends the circus because he resents the clowns. How can a person get through life devoid of serious responsibilities? This is the question he would ask them if ever he was introduced. He likes the animals though, the bigger the better. The elephants especially, mainly because he sees himself reflected in their personalities. In his eyes they seem like patient and very intelligent creatures, not prone to fits of panic or illusion. If only he knew the truth!
Gerrie:
Very spelling-aware in lieu of the continual misspellings of his name, which in turn has made him quite careful in life, Gerrie's height gives him a certain presence and his children are generally well-educated. 
Question: Is Gerrie similar to David Lee Roth? (Ex-lead singer of a band called Van Halen. Google him if you’ve never heard of him)
Anyway…

Answer: No.
Gerrit: A very patient home builder/renovator. Yes, the plans look great, the weather seems to be fine for the next few months and money isn't an issue, but unforeseen mishaps are a CERTAINTY. Gerrit is very aware of this, which is why, no matter what happens, he's always watchful about how things are progressing. He never ever gets ahead of himself, even in the bedroom, which some might consider a pity.
Gerry: Gerry is not as outlandish as one might think. He walks with an easy gait and he has the capacity to marvel at the tiny things as well as the large. At his core he is a calm and searching soul who listens and observes, offering advice only when asked or if a situation or person obviously requires it.
Gery:
I don't know he does it, really, but Gery's life seems to be remarkably devoid of boring rigmarole. Maybe it's that hard 'g' at the start of his name that sets him off in a direction quickly and without hesitation, and let's face it, hesitation is the harbinger of red-tape and useless caffuffle. Know what I mean?

(Good mates with Dick.)
Giaan: Giaan is deep. He designs sunglasses. He even sleeps with them on.
Giacomo: Giacomo stands on the deck of his Spanish Galleon with a wench in one hand and a telescope in the other, searching the horizon for any generally irresponsible mischief to be had. (Like Nick a little later on, he’s barely heard of the Tax Office.)
Gianluca: The passionate and gentle Italian man, whether he’s Italian or not. His parents might just love Italy, which happens sometimes.
Gib: Smooth. Gib doesn’t mess around with useless deeds or thoughts and he only falls to pieces if kept inside for too long where there is a good chance he will suddenly turn into some kind of caged animal. He’d die if he had to spend a winter in Sweden, although, having said that, he’d probably satiate his sense of adventure by stealing away with a pack of huskies and a dog sled where he’d quite happily feast on raw venison until he got bored with the lack of girls to chase – or be chased by.
Gibbo:
Option A: A big, beer drinking, chauvinistic Queenslander/Texan.

Option B: The name of a colourful old blanket that is tossed over the back of a donkey in a Spaghetti Western. As such, he’s an ideal contact if you intend to carry guns, drugs or tequila.
Gibbs: No, he's no flower posy. He's more like the shovel in the hands of a gardener who knows how to wield one. Gibbs shares a joke and he's a laid-back character, but when he gets down to work - and it can't be too technical or complex - he puts his head down and tries as best he can. Drinks too much.
Gideon: Musician, artist, hippy, philosopher, grave digger or glass blower: this is where you will find him.
Gidz: Gidz is a cynical, if not a very humorous individual. If watching an ad on TV that he detests, he will leap to his feet and swear that he’ll never buy that product again. And he never will.
Gil: Gil inhabits one of those bodies in which is it nigh' impossible to ascertain what he does for a living. For instance, he might be so funny and gregarious that you would presume he's a stand-up comedian when in fact he is a civil engineer. Or maybe he's a plumber in his day job, with mud and dirt perpetually underneath his fingernails, who has a world famous butterfly collection? Perhaps he's a mild-mannered dog breeder who is awkward in large groups of humans, and who on the weekend turns into an avid skydiver? I suppose Gil never feels the need to boast, we're not sure, but he's certainly worth following.
Gilbert: Has any one person gotten away with more? Sure, someone like Alby might but he's quite open about his irresponsibilites. Gilbert on the other hand slips around situations like an unseen snake, whisking away money, goods and womens' hearts like its nobodies business. How do you do that Gilbert?
Gilby:
Defence attache, is his job title. We can't tell you what he really does - it's top secret - and you'd never consider him someone who would do such a job, only because the car he drives, the women he hangs out with and number of famous people in his phone are more akin to a Hollywood A-lister.
Has he been shot at? Yes.
He can't remember the last time he was bored.
Giles: "I say, George, do you mind dropping the Maserati off for a service this week? And if you don't mind, I think it's time to dust off the 'roller. Do you mind doing that for this afternoon?.....Splendid."
Gilles: What is it with Frenchmen? They talk loudly, frown heavily at things that are inconsequential to most people and this one - well, to say he has a wandering eye would be an understatement.
Gilly: As a Japanese girl in past life he has a fetish for Asian Kung-Fu movies. Gilly rhymes with ‘Hii-yaaaa!!!’, after all. And he’s one of the few people on earth whose smile is actually wider than their face, which aids him to be one of the world’s truly generous men.
Gimp: The Gimp loves burrowing down inside his hole and meditating. In a good mood he ponders things like love and the synchronicity of the universe. In a bad one he licks his lips and conjures up notions of perfect evil.
Gino:
Gino is the only man to work at the tax department who has been investigated by the tax department. On his gravestone will be the following epitaph:

Keep your friends close and your enemies closer.
Giovanni: How can one person lie so much and yet be loved as much as they are? We're still trying to come to terms with that one. Just don't make him the captain of any large ship because it'll all end in tears. Trust me.
Glen: Glen is like the state of California in that he is affluent, good company (generally) and occasionally ‘out there’, but through the middle of him runs something akin to the San Andreas fault. The question is, when and/or will the entire state suddenly tear apart and slip into the Pacific Ocean? Who knows.....maybe it won’t?
Glenn: Glenn is like the state of California in that he is affluent, good company (generally) and occasionally ‘out there’, but through the middle of him runs something akin to the San Andreas fault. The question is, when and/or will the entire state suddenly tear apart and slip into the Pacific Ocean? Who knows.....maybe it won’t? (And yes, that's right, the double N doesn't change a thing, apart from highlighting the fact that at least one of parents is completely fucking dyslexic.)
Glenrowan: Nice guy. He's a snob, sure, but he's okay.
Glenville: Similar to a very large and expensive ocean liner which has lost the use of its rudder, Glenville moves reasonably slowly. A fine looking vessel however, and we expect the salvagers will make a killing. (ie: Glenville may very well inherit a bucket of money, but unlike the previous generation who earned it, he will do a fine job of wasting the lot.)
Googie: Googie is a light-hearted soul who doesn’t actively decide anything at all. Years ago he read a book called The Dice Man and in allowing ‘the universe’ to dictate how his life unfolds, it has never been the same since. God only knows what he’s up to today...
Gordo: A large, bustling man who does very little in a meek fashion. He’s up for a hair-brain scheme, he’s up for a bit of hanky panky, and he’ll try anything once. 95% of Gordos have a kind heart, so none of his carry on carries any malice, praise be the lord.
Gordon: Gordon is a big personality and a great hulk of a man in body and/or spirit. He’s rollicking fun at dinner parties, for instance, until he gets pissed and tries to lift up all the girls’ skirts.
Gough: A fierce competitor who is outraged by acts of prejudice against the innocent. Sure, his sense of humour might need some work, but it's not his fault. In a past life he was once slayed on a Scottish moor defending his clan and so how do you reckon he was going to turn out?
Goughie:
Goughie rhymes with, ‘Jesus, that was close..’, as well as, ‘Anyone seen the remote?’
Overall, Goughie gets on with life in a no-nonsense fashion, cruising with the luck that he seems to generate himself. His approach has paid off because the result is a contented bloke who is more than happy to put on his girlfriends’ bathers at a moment’s notice.
Goulbourne: Born on the land, Goulbourne knows a lot more about soil, crops, wethers and motors than the latest theories on the whereabouts of the G-spot. Indeed, Goulbourne, mate, do you even know what a clitoris does?…..We’ll leave it with you. Good luck.
Goz: Like a big and somewhat dopey Red Setter, Goz has more friends than he knows what to do with. His girlfriends/partners need to be funny as well, and if they can hold their liquor then all the better. Goz is easily pleased but laughter in his life is a must. His needs are relatively simple and he is good with his hands, so if you have one we suggest you take him out in the countryside and let him run free for a while…maybe throw him a big juicy bone when he’s finished.
Graco: Probably too intelligent for his own good. Graco is extremely charismatic and he does play games, although he only does it to give himself something to do because most people bore him, shitless.
Grady: Like his female counterpart, Grady seems to appear from out of nowhere. He's nowhere near as compassionate as her though. We suspect he's a vampire, which would explain things. True, he's not the only vampire out there, but he's safe enough.
Graeme: Graeme is like water. In the driest continent on Earth, therefore, he is an iconic figure because he provides energy and life without any fanfare. I’m not sure where any of us would be without him.
Graham: Graham is basically the same as his brother (Graeme) but he isn’t as good at getting his hands dirty.
Grant: Grant is potent and single-minded. He’s often misread as a bully or a grouch but that’s not right – he’s just doing what it takes.
Granville: An eccentric Scottish Lord who either drinks whisky while playing golf, or drinks whisky while shooting peasants…..oops...I mean, pheasants.
Gratias: Gratias is as quiet as a mouse until he gets pissed with the boys.
Greg:
Option A: Plain like a pancake without anything on it. Greg is so plain, in fact, he is occasionally a little perplexed by his own boring normalness. But don’t think for a second that if push comes to shove he can’t (and won’t) stand up for what he believes in. (In a past life he was a pilot of an RAF Lancaster bomber which was shot up and in flames over Germany, and he refused to bail-out until each of his surviving crew members had made it out first…)

Option B: The current president of the National Association for Nudists, which proves Greg is rarely as dull as you might imagine.
Gregg: Ever seen the first Independence Day movie? Anyway, Gregg is just like the maths professor who saves the world. He watches all the fools squawk and yell and carry on, clambering for either attention, love or money, until he thinks everyone is ready to hear what he has secretly discovered. Usually, no one else has thought of it. That aside, throughout nearly all aspects of his life Gregg retains a splendid, happy demeanour, he's rarely rushed and he's always on the lookout for anything weird or kinky. You can give him shit about his name if you like, but he'd just think of you in the same way we would - you're probably a buffoon and therefore worthy of being either ignored or pitied. Have a nice day.
Gregor: Never judge a book by its cover. An intellect of gargantuan proportions lies undiscovered here, so what if he has Asperger's Syndrome? Society and its rules are usually full of crap anyway. Remember this: Gregor is here to help and here to help others laugh as well, no matter what his profession.
Gregory: Gregory died out in the early 80’s when the ozone layer started to disappear. It was probably a blessing.
Greig: The aloof stalker who keeps a stash of Rohipnol in his cupboard.
Griff: House painter. Funny as a whip. At the end of the day you can see him out the back of the house laughing with his crew. They're all covered in paint and they all smoke - as if the paint fumes aren't harmful enough - but that's okay. The day is over and they all aim to be better men next week. Whose shout is it anyway?
Griffin: Griffin seems to deal with life as if he is a Sultan Prince who has been magically tranported into the body of a young western middle class man, who needs a job but hasn't got one, and who really doesn't want one.
Grof: Grof is like one of those big poodles that, when he looks at  you, you'd swear is actually a small man in a very hairy jacket. Funny guy. Loves a cuddle.
Grub: Well, yes, he’ll get his hands dirty, but you’d be hard pressed to find a person who works harder. He thinks on his feet, has excellent common sense, can read people like a book almost on first sight and is incredibly loyal. In a past life he was head engineer/armorer for a bomber squadron in England, during World War 2, and his heart broke every time one of his planes didn't made it back.
Guido: Guido is one twisted mother fucker, be it sexually or otherwise.
Guillermo: Guillermo arrives like a three-piece band on a Saturday night: loud, colourful and impossible to ignore. He paints, he cooks, he plays the guitar badly but with tremendous conviction, and he has strong opinions about all three. He is not a natural leader (he'd rather you just did it his way, without the meetings), but he is generous with his laughter and his wine. Argue with him at your peril, then hug him at the end of the night. He'll have forgotten all about it.
Guiseppe: A dreamer. We suspect he'd like to be a realist but we're glad he's not. Guiseppe.
Guitar: Yeah, but can he play? Or is he so sick of the expectation that he never wants to look at a guitar ever again?...
Gunner: A good team man in any sports club.
Gunter: Possibly Dutch, Gunter is a marvellous specimen. He approaches every moment with fresh eyes and ears, and his dogged optimism would be worth millions if one could only bottle it. And he has a genuine, welcoming laugh.
Guppy: No hidden tricks here, folks. Guppy plays pretty hard, he begrudgingly works pretty hard, and all in all he’s worth his due.
Gus: Gus was a roo shooter for years until he discovered how much he enjoyed being at sea, and where he truly discovered the effects of gravity and momentum. The last I heard he was driving fishing boats in either the Southern Ocean or the Irish Sea, but he's always been good with engines.
Gustav: He looks and sounds gruff but trust me, Gustav is just a big, playful teddy bear.
Guy: 17 years old no matter how old he is, Guy has a terrible time trying to explain why and how a 41 year old man has as many wet dreams as he does. In life, his decisions are often rash and he’s a hopeless lover, but it’s not all bad because he’s one of the few men that has the capacity to autofellate. Disregarding his sexual prowess, Guy is a wonderful harbinger of change and therefore one of the most optimistic people in the room.
Gyrin: First things first, we need to get a DNA sample from him just to confirm our theory, but he’s no fool. If Gyrin suspects we’re onto him he’ll be off like a shot, and it’s not as if he doesn’t know how to blend into the background. He also knows how to break the rules, as most alien creatures here on Earth are prone to do. But you won’t find Gyrin conducting his human-observational studies way out in the middle of nowhere. Shit no. You’ll find him up to his neck in some kind of absurd social life where the spotlight isn’t far off, and where he’s managed to convince everyone he’s a brilliant human artist/raconteur. Funny thing is, he actually is, and he doesn’t mind you knowing about it either, bless his alien cotton socks. Amen.
Gæton: Well-travelled, artistic, educated and competitive – be it in the kitchen or as a downhill skier – Gæton tends to live large.
